marks.gloss_en: דכתיב ופרץ גדר ישכנו נחש -- one who breaches a fence is bitten by a snake
אין רבי -- he had broken Rav Yitzchak bar Bisna's decree by bringing myrtle and palm to a wedding house with a drum

a certain bar kasha of Pumbedita was bitten by a snake; there were thirteen white she-asses in Pumbedita, they tore them all open and all were found trefa; there was one on the far side of Pumbedita, and by the time they went to bring it a lion had eaten it

one whom a snake has wound round -- let him go down into water, upturn a basket over his head and work it off him; when it goes up onto [the basket] let him throw it into the water and come up and away

a woman whom a snake has seen, who does not know whether it has set its mind on her -- let her take off her garments and throw them before it: if it wraps itself in them its mind is on her, and if not, not
what is her remedy? let her have intercourse before it
תנינא: כל המשקין שותה -- 'drinks' are what people drink, and people do not drink urine (kind svara: no kind exists for תנינא)
the mishna: all foods a person may eat for healing [on Shabbat]
what is a kos ikarin? R' Yochanan: let one bring a zuz-weight of Alexandrian gum, a zuz-weight of alum and a zuz-weight of garden saffron, and grind them together
the mishna: [all drinks he may drink] except palm-water
Rav Yosef: Egyptian zitom is a third barley, a third saffron (kurtemei), and a third salt
